info.title: Marinade's Delegation Strategy API
info.description: This API serves data about validators and their performance.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description:
Case-insensitive text search. A client is kept when its own name matches or one of its
block engines does, and its block engines are then served whole.

parameters.name: order_field
parameters.description: Orders the clients, and the block engines inside each one by the same column.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Applies to the clients only; a client always arrives with all of its block engines.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Case-insensitive text search over the provider name.

get.description: Mainnet client releases and the two version floors, as three lists: what was published (`releases`), what the Solana Foundation Delegation Program required (`sfdp_floors`), and what the cluster's feature gates required (`feature_gate_floors`).

parameters.name: client
parameters.description: Client lineage, e.g. `agave` or `frankendancer`. An unknown one serves an empty list.

parameters.name: since_epoch
parameters.description: Lower-bound epoch, inclusive. Each list is filtered on its own epoch.

parameters.name: order_direction
parameters.description: Orders `releases` by publish time and both floor lists by the epoch they took effect.

parameters.name: report_id
parameters.description: Scoring run ID in format epoch.run_number

parameters.name: query
parameters.description:
Text search over validator name, vote account and identity. To also search other
properties (datacenter location), set `search_properties=true`.

parameters.name: query_incident_free
parameters.description: `true` keeps the validators whose `incidents` array comes back empty, `false` the rest. Shaped by incident related query options.

parameters.name: query_incident_types
parameters.description: Comma-separated incident types to serve: `Downtime`, `BlockProduction`, `CommissionSpike`, `RunningLateClientVersion`, `Sandwich` (defaults to just `Downtime`).

parameters.name: min_incident_downtime_seconds
parameters.description: Minimum downtime in seconds for a `DOWN` interval to read as an incident. Shorter intervals are restart noise, and reach neither the `incidents` array nor `order_field=incidents` nor `query_incident_free`. Only applies to the downtime incident type.

parameters.name: min_incident_missed_slots
parameters.description: Minimum missed leader slots for a skipped epoch to read as an incident. Defaults to 4, minimum 4.

parameters.name: min_incident_leader_slots
parameters.description: Minimum leader slots an epoch needs before its block production is judged. Defaults to 64, minimum 64.

parameters.name: min_incident_sandwich_rate
parameters.description: Minimum 30-day sandwich rate in percent. Only raises the bar.

parameters.name: incident_window_epochs
parameters.description: Epochs back the `incidents` array reaches, counting the newest reported epoch itself. Defaults to 90; above 90 — the whole window the cache holds — answers 400. Unrelated to `epochs`, which sizes `epoch_stats`.

parameters.name: query_provider
parameters.description: Exact, case-insensitive match on a `key` from `/providers`. `Unknown` selects the validators with no recorded provider.

parameters.name: query_client
parameters.description: Exact, case-insensitive match on a `key` from `/clients`. `Unknown` selects the validators with no recorded client.

parameters.name: query_block_engine
parameters.description: A vendor slug from `block_engine_vendors`, such as `bam`. `none` takes the validators running no block engine. Case-insensitive. Pair it with `query_client` to address one `/clients` child row.

parameters.name: search_properties
parameters.description:
When true, `query` also matches datacenter location fields (country, city) in addition to
validator name, vote account and identity.

parameters.name: with_operator_groups
parameters.description: `true` groups the validators into operator blocks, returns the `operators` aggregates beside them, and pages over those top-level rows rather than validators.

parameters.name: vote_account
parameters.description: Vote account or identity of the validator

get.description: Per-epoch performance, downtime and PSR settlement events for a validator. `settlements[].reason` / `.meta` are raw upstream JSON.

parameters.name: vote_account
parameters.description: Vote account or identity of the validator

parameters.name: query_from_epoch
parameters.description: Lower-bound epoch (inclusive). Mutually exclusive with `query_from_date`. Defaults to the last 90 epochs.

parameters.name: query_from_date
parameters.description: Lower-bound date (RFC3339), resolved to the first epoch ending on/after it. Mutually exclusive with `query_from_epoch`.

400.description: Invalid query params (query_from_epoch / query_from_date are mutually exclusive, or query_from_date is outside the recorded epoch range)

404.description: No validator found for the given vote account or identity

get.description: Take rate per epoch for a validator. Returns the whole stored history unless bounded by a query parameter. `epoch_start_at` and `epoch_end_at` are null for epochs whose boundaries are not recorded.

BlockProductionDetail.description: What a validator produced of its leader slots in one epoch, and the bar it was held to.

cluster_skip_rate.description: The epoch's cluster-wide skip rate, over the validators that were evaluable that epoch.

counts_as_incident.description:
Whether these numbers count as an incident.
Affected by query params `min_incident_missed_slots` and `min_incident_leader_slots`.

threshold.description: The bar `skip_rate` had to clear that epoch, as a fraction.

ClientRelease.description: The newest release of a client lineage.

FeatureGateFloor.description: A version the cluster's feature gates required, and the epoch it started requiring it.

validator.description: Vote account of the member the incident is on.

GroupIncidentRecord.description: A member's incident as its group carries it, `incident_type` and all.

GroupIncidents.description: A group's incidents, as records or as their count. Serializes as a JSON array or a JSON number.

GroupLocation.description: Validator stats on the level of a datacenter location.

oneOf.description: One DOWN interval from the uptimes table.

The epoch's block production, whenever there was any to measure. Breach or not: this
record exists because the validator went down, and these are the numbers alongside it.
A closed epoch the validator was up for but produced too few of its leader slots in.

An epoch the validator raised its inflation commission in, to
[`crate::incidents::COMMISSION_SPIKE_THRESHOLD_PERCENTAGE`] or above.
Excludes MEV and block-revenue commissions.

changed_at.description: When the raised rate was first sampled.

oneOf.description:
A run of epochs with a 30-day sandwich rate far above the cluster median. The numbers
below come from `peak_epoch`.

blocks_produced.description: Blocks over the 30-day window the rate is measured on, not over the epoch.

sandwich_rate_60d.description: Null before epoch 820: upstream published only the 30d rate then.

threshold.description: The bar `sandwich_rate_30d` had to clear, in percent.

oneOf.description: Measured against adoption in the same lineage, not the floors `/releases` publishes.

newer_stake_share.description: Share of the lineage's stake on a strictly newer version, as a fraction.

newer_version_stake_shares.description: Every version above this one, newest first. The shares sum to `newer_stake_share`.

IncidentRecord.description: One incident on a validator. `incident_type` says which kind, and which fields are present.

available_epoch.description: Epoch the release was published in, resolved from `released_at` against the epochs we hold.

client_version.description: As the client reports it in gossip, e.g. `4.2.2` or `0.1106.40201`.

ResponseClients.description: Clients as a two-level tree: one row per client, its block engines underneath.

ResponseProviders.description: Groups by hosting organisation (`dc_aso`); the data never resolves the building.

net_apy_updated_at.description:
When apy-api last answered for the net APY the rates are derived from. Older than a few
minutes means those values are being reused because that API is failing.

total_activated_stake.description: Activated stake of every validator counted, in lamports — the denominator behind `stake_share`.

rewards_block.description: block production rewards based on signature count and priority fees

slots_per_year.description:
nominal slots per year in force in each epoch, the divisor behind rewards_inflation_est;
includes the running epoch, which has no rewards_inflation_est entry yet

bond_flags_updated_at.description: When validator-bonds last answered for the `verified`/`protected` flags. Older than a few minutes means the flags are being reused because that API is failing.

net_apy_updated_at.description: When apy-api last answered for `net_apy`. Older than a few minutes means those values are being reused because that API is failing.

operators.description:
Operator rows, ordered by `order_field`, present only under `with_operator_groups`. Aggregated
over the validators matching the query and filters, so a row describes the validators served
under it.

total_activated_stake.description:
Activated stake of every validator matching the query, in lamports — the denominator behind the
operator rows' `stake_share`. Summing the rows does not recover it: a validator belonging to no
operator counts here and has no row. Present only under `with_operator_groups`.

total_count.description:
Number of rows matching the query and filters, before `offset`/`limit`: validators, or
top-level rows under `with_operator_groups`.

reason.description: Raw upstream JSON tagged enum, e.g. `"Bidding"` or `{"ProtectedEvent":{...}}`.

SfdpFloor.description: A version the Solana Foundation Delegation Program required, and the epoch it started requiring it.

expected_take_rate.description: Take rate implied by the epoch's commissions, weighted by the epoch's reward mix.

block_engine_vendors.description:
The vendor slug of each entry in `block_engines`, in the same order. `query_block_engine`
takes a slug from here.

block_engines.description: Block engines paired with this client, from the group's own children.

oneOf.description: Null when the lineage has published no release we know of.

version_spread.description: Stake share per version string as the nodes report it, biggest first. Unbucketed.

ValidatorClientGroupRecord.description: A client lineage, as the parent rows of `/clients` serve it.

block_revenue_collector.description: SIMD-0232 account this validator's block revenue is paid into. Null on a pre-v4 vote state, where agave credits the leader identity instead. Read from the vote state that built the leader schedule, so a sample taken now predicts the *next* epoch's block revenue, not this one's.

block_revenue_collector_is_identity.description: Whether `block_revenue_collector` still points at the current identity, which is its default. Null on a pre-v4 vote state. False does **not** imply a deliberate redirect: agave stopped re-syncing this field to the identity once SIMD-0232 activated, so changing identity leaves it on the old one.

block_revenue_collector_shared_count.description: How many vote accounts in this epoch name the same `block_revenue_collector`, this one included. Carries the same no-consent caveat as `inflation_rewards_collector_shared_count`, but not its attribution loss: block revenue is deposited per block rather than merged into one epoch reward row.

block_revenue_commission_bps.description: Block-revenue commission in basis points. Inert until SIMD-0123 activates, and 10000 by default on a vote state migrated to v4, which reads as "the validator keeps all of it" rather than as an inflation rate. Null on a pre-v4 vote state.

client_id.description: Numeric Solana Foundation client id decoded from `client_id_raw`; null when the answering RPC rendered a name absent from our registry. `client_vendor` and `client_lineage` are derived from it, but stay null for an id the registry does not know.

client_id_raw.description: Literal `getClusterNodes.clientId`, rendered by the answering RPC's own table so the same node may report `Rakurai` or `Unknown(8)`; use `client_id` instead.

client_label.description: Client label to display, never null: the lineage, plus the vendor's modification of it when there is one, e.g. `Agave + JitoBAM` or `Frankendancer`. `Unknown` for a client the registry does not know.

client_lineage.description: Which upstream codebase `client_id` is built from: `agave`, `firedancer`, `frankendancer` or `sig`.

client_name.description: Client name to display, never null: the Solana Foundation registry name of `client_id`, e.g. `Rakurai` or `Agave Bam`, and `Unknown` for a client the registry does not know. See `client_id_raw` for what the node actually reported.

client_vendor.description: Who ships the binary, derived from `client_id`, collapsing a vendor's per-lineage ids (`HarmonicAgave` + `HarmonicFiredancer` -> `harmonic`).

commission_effective_source.description: Where `commission_effective` came from: `reward_row` is the rate the runtime told us it applied, `vote_state` is the last rate sampled from vote state during the epoch — the close sample for a validator still voting, the sample from when it left the vote set otherwise — which is what remains since SIMD-0232 removed the rate from the reward rows. Null for an epoch closed before this was recorded, and for a validator with neither source.

commission_max_observed.description: The epoch's ceiling and floor across every commission sample and the applied rate. Both fold in `commission_effective`, which is a whole-percent projection rounded up from basis points, so either bound can read up to 1pp above the rate actually charged.

inflation_rewards_collector.description: SIMD-0232 account this validator's inflation commission is paid into. Null on a pre-v4 vote state, where agave has no collector to read and credits the vote account itself — null is not "the vote account", it is "no collector recorded". Sampled from live vote state, so it predicts this epoch's payout, which lands in the first block of the next epoch.

inflation_rewards_collector_redirected.description: Whether `inflation_rewards_collector` points somewhere other than the vote account, so a consumer need not diff pubkeys. Null on a pre-v4 vote state. Unlike the block-revenue side this does mean a deliberate redirect: a vote account's own address never changes, and the only way to move this collector is the `UpdateCommissionCollector` instruction.

inflation_rewards_collector_shared_count.description: How many vote accounts in this epoch name the same `inflation_rewards_collector`, this one included. More than one means the runtime merges their commissions into a single reward row and the per-validator split is not recoverable from the ledger. **Not a relationship between those validators**: SIMD-0232 asks a collector for no signature of its own, so anyone can point a throwaway vote account at somebody else's collector. Never key an identity or an operator grouping on a collector.

inflation_rewards_commission_bps.description: Inflation commission in basis points as the vote state carried it. Authoritative where the whole-percent fields are a `div_ceil` projection of it. Set on every vote state version: agave synthesizes `commission * 100` on a pre-v4 account, so this is the rate it applies either way — read `inflation_rewards_commission_bps_is_v4` to tell a rate the validator set in basis points from that projection.

inflation_rewards_commission_bps_is_v4.description: Whether `inflation_rewards_commission_bps` came from a v4 vote state, where a validator can set a fraction of a percent, rather than being agave's `commission * 100` projection of a whole-percent rate. Null where nothing was sampled.

pending_delegator_rewards.description: Inflation rewards accrued to this vote account and not yet distributed to its delegators. Null on a pre-v4 vote state.

ValidatorGroupNode.description: One client — `Agave`, `Frankendancer`, `Firedancer` etc. — with the block engines it runs with.

ValidatorGroupRecord.description: Group can be a hosting provider, validator client or node operator

asns.description: Stake-sorted. One hosting organisation commonly announces from several.

client_mix.description: Stake share per client lineage, biggest first.

ValidatorProviderGroupRecord.description: A hosting provider, as `/providers` serves it.

client_id.description: Numeric Solana Foundation client id decoded from `client_id_raw`; null when the answering RPC rendered a name absent from our registry. `client_vendor` and `client_lineage` are derived from it, but stay null for an id the registry does not know.

client_id_raw.description: Literal `getClusterNodes.clientId`, rendered by the answering RPC's own table so the same node may report `Rakurai` or `Unknown(8)`; use `client_id` instead.

client_label.description: Client label to display, never null: the lineage, plus the vendor's modification of it when there is one, e.g. `Agave + JitoBAM` or `Frankendancer`. `Unknown` for a client the registry does not know.

client_lineage.description: Which upstream codebase `client_id` is built from: `agave`, `firedancer`, `frankendancer` or `sig`.

client_name.description: Client name to display, never null: the Solana Foundation registry name of `client_id`, e.g. `Rakurai` or `Agave Bam`, and `Unknown` for a client the registry does not know. See `client_id_raw` for what the node actually reported.

client_vendor.description: Who ships the binary, derived from `client_id`, collapsing a vendor's per-lineage ids (`HarmonicAgave` + `HarmonicFiredancer` -> `harmonic`).

commission_effective_source.description: See `ValidatorEpochStats::commission_effective_source`. Projected from the newest closed epoch, alongside `commission_effective` itself.

expected_take_rate.description: What the validator's current fee settings imply it keeps, as a fraction: its inflation, MEV and block-reward commissions weighted by the cluster reward mix. Forward-looking where `avg_take_rate` measures realized rewards, so two validators on the same fee settings read the same here regardless of size or block-production luck. Taking no commission anywhere floors it at the cluster block share, not at 0, because block rewards go wholly to the producer unless it also shares them through Jito's PriorityFeeDistribution. The inflation commission is the worse of `commission_max_observed` and `commission_advertised`, so a validator that only advertises a low rate early in the epoch reads at the rate it actually charges. Null for a validator whose commission is unknown on both.

inflation_rewards_commission_bps.description: See `ValidatorEpochStats::inflation_rewards_commission_bps`. Read from the newest epoch sampled, which is the open one, as is every vote-state field below it. It therefore does not pair with `commission_effective` above, which is a closed epoch's rate: a validator that moved its commission this epoch reads two different rates here.

net_apy.description: Latest point of the apy-api 14-day rolling staker APY, a fraction like `avg_apy` but MEV-inclusive where `avg_apy` is inflation-only. Null for a validator apy-api has no rewards data for.

operator.description: Node operator from the operators CSV; null for a vote account the file does not list.

protected.description: As listed by the validator-bonds `/validators/protected` endpoint, which owns the rule.

stake_delta_7d.description:
Stake gained since the epoch the group rows measure their own 7-day delta against, so the two
reconcile. Null when history does not reach back that far.

client_id.description: Numeric Solana Foundation client id decoded from `client_id_raw`; null when the answering RPC rendered a name absent from our registry. `client_vendor` and `client_lineage` are derived from it, but stay null for an id the registry does not know.

client_id_raw.description: Literal `getClusterNodes.clientId`, rendered by the answering RPC's own table so the same node may report `Rakurai` or `Unknown(8)`; use `client_id` instead.

client_label.description: Client label to display, never null: the lineage, plus the vendor's modification of it when there is one, e.g. `Agave + JitoBAM` or `Frankendancer`. `Unknown` for a client the registry does not know.

client_lineage.description: Which upstream codebase `client_id` is built from: `agave`, `firedancer`, `frankendancer` or `sig`.

client_name.description: Client name to display, never null: the Solana Foundation registry name of `client_id`, e.g. `Rakurai` or `Agave Bam`, and `Unknown` for a client the registry does not know. See `client_id_raw` for what the node actually reported.

client_vendor.description: Who ships the binary, derived from `client_id`, collapsing a vendor's per-lineage ids (`HarmonicAgave` + `HarmonicFiredancer` -> `harmonic`).

share.description: Share of the lineage's stake in that epoch, as a fraction.
